actions.fingerprint_skip: a governed builder's seal step stays fingerprint-gated (semantic DB fingerprint + declared input set): unchanged inputs skip the rebuild entirely, so the windowed emit runs only when the data actually moved
actions.peak_bound: a peak-RSS bound is recorded per builder; a re-proof whose measured windowed peak exceeds the bound fails the proof
actions.proof_gate: the windowed path is trusted only after a rig A/B proof: windowed vs the classic (un-windowed) builder on identical inputs, every output byte-identical, hashes recorded below; any later edit to a governed builder changes its sha256 and the A1.5 gate goes RED until a fresh proof is recorded
actions.release_before_emit: the in-memory row set is released before the downstream document emit, so the emit peak never stacks the row set under the document build
actions.streamed_writes: emitted bytes stream through a bounded chunk writer; no whole-output array or string is materialized beside the row set
actions.streaming_digests: digests are computed by per-row streaming hash updates; no whole-set canonical string
actions.twin_sweep: every seat of a governed builder changes in the same pass and stays byte-identical (sha256 equality across seats, enforced here and by check-twins.js TW-1)
actions.windowed_reads: aggregate and verification reads over a full table run in ORDER BY windows of bounded size; no read materializes the whole table

rule: A builder is GOVERNED by this step when its emit phase materializes a data structure whose size scales with a full estate table — the row set, the statement list, a whole-set canonical string, or an aggregate pass over the table — so its peak memory grows with the census instead of with the batch delta. A governed builder may not run in a production seal until its windowed path carries a rig proof recorded here. A new builder that reads or emits a full estate table joins this registry BEFORE its first production seal.
